components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 他把老师的话传达给了全班同学。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ lǎoshī de huà chuándá gěi le quánbān tóngxué.
example.english: He conveyed the teacher's words to the whole class.
example.fact: The Pony Express relayed mail across nearly 2,000 miles of the American West in about 10 days, with riders swapping fresh horses every 10-15 miles — a relay system that beat the stagecoach by more than half. It shut down in 1861 almost as soon as the transcontinental telegraph could convey messages across the same distance in minutes instead of days.

components.note: 以 traces back to an early pictograph of a person bending forward with an arm extended, as if lifting or holding a tool; the sense of putting something to use broadened into 'to use, by means of, in order to.'
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'
刂 (a knife, related to 刀) — cutting and arranging pieces in order ties to 列's meaning 'row, line, to arrange'

example.hanzi: 以色列位于中东地区。
example.pinyin: Yǐsèliè wèiyú Zhōngdōng dìqū.
example.english: Israel is located in the Middle East region.
example.fact: The Dead Sea, on Israel's border, sits about 430 meters below sea level — the lowest point on Earth's land surface. Its water is roughly ten times saltier than the ocean, which is why swimmers float on the surface almost without trying.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 镇 originally referred to a heavy metal weight used to press something down, later extending to 'garrison town.'
真 (zhēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 镇's reading zhèn, differing only in tone.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 面对危险，她表现得非常镇定。
example.pinyin: Miànduì wēixiǎn, tā biǎoxiàn de fēicháng zhèndìng.
example.english: Facing danger, she remained very calm.
example.fact: Elite free-divers train to stay calm underwater by triggering the mammalian dive reflex, which can slow the human heart rate from a resting ~70 beats per minute to below 20. The reflex, shared with seals and whales, redirects blood to the heart and brain to conserve oxygen during a breath-hold.

components.note: 门 (gate, door) shows 阁 relates to a type of building with an entrance.
各 (gè) gives a sound close to gé, differing mainly in tone.
木 (wood) — buildings were traditionally framed with wood.
娄 (lóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 楼.

example.hanzi: 我们把旧家具放在阁楼里。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bǎ jiù jiājù fàng zài gélóu lǐ.
example.english: We put the old furniture in the attic.
example.fact: During World War II, Anne Frank and seven others hid for two years in a cramped attic annex above an Amsterdam canal-house office, accessible only through a door hidden behind a swinging bookcase. Anne's diary, kept there, has since been translated into more than 70 languages.

meanings: to greet sb by word or action

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
扌 (hand) — suggests a gesture, a beckoning motion.
召 depicts a call or summons — a hand gesture calling someone over gave 招 its meaning 'to beckon, to recruit.'
口 (mouth) — 呼 describes an action of the mouth, such as calling out or breathing.
乎 (hū) gives the sound — an exact match with 呼.

example.hanzi: 邻居见面都会打招呼。
example.pinyin: Línjū jiànmiàn dōu huì dǎ zhāohu.
example.english: Neighbors greet each other when they meet.
example.fact: Ancient Greek funerary reliefs from the 5th century BC already depict figures clasping right hands, one of the earliest known artistic records of the handshake. One theory holds the gesture proved a person wasn't concealing a weapon, turning a safety check into a lasting greeting.

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — many early villages were built among or from trees and wood
寸 (cùn) gives a sound close to 村's reading cūn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
广 (shelter/building) — 庄 originally referred to farm buildings or a manor house.
壯 (zhuàng) gives a sound close to zhuāng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 这个村庄坐落在山脚下。
example.pinyin: Zhège cūnzhuāng zuòluò zài shānjiǎo xià.
example.english: This village sits at the foot of a mountain.
example.fact: The town of Jericho, in the Jordan Valley, has archaeological evidence of continuous habitation stretching back more than 11,000 years, making it one of the oldest known permanently inhabited settlements on Earth. Its famous stone tower, dated to around 8000 BC, still predates the pyramids by millennia.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.
巳 (a place) — the destination being pointed toward, giving 导 its meaning 'to lead, guide, direct.'

example.hanzi: 记者报导了这次事故的经过。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě bàodǎo le zhè cì shìgù de jīngguò.
example.english: The reporter reported on how the accident unfolded.
example.fact: Washington Post reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein spent two years, from 1972 to 1974, piecing together the Watergate scandal from anonymous sources and leaked documents. Their reporting eventually helped force President Richard Nixon's resignation, the only time a US president has left office that way.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — reflects 阿's original meaning related to a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 阿's reading ā
宀 (roof) — 富 relates to a well-stocked household, prosperous under its own roof
畐 (fú) gives a sound close to 富's reading fù, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
氵 (water) — 汗 names sweat, a bodily fluid.
干 (gān) shares the rhyme -an with hàn, though the initial has drifted from g- to h- over time.

example.hanzi: 阿富汗是一个多山的国家。
example.pinyin: Āfùhàn shì yī gè duōshān de guójiā.
example.english: Afghanistan is a mountainous country.
example.fact: The Sar-e-Sang mines in Afghanistan's Badakhshan province have produced lapis lazuli, a deep-blue semi-precious stone, for over 6,000 years. Ground into pigment, that lapis traveled along ancient trade routes to color the eyes of Egyptian pharaohs' masks and, later, European Renaissance paintings.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.
日 (sun) — 晰 describes something as clear and bright as sunlight.
析 (xī) gives the sound — an exact match with 晰.

example.hanzi: 这张照片非常清晰。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn fēicháng qīngxī.
example.english: This photo is very clear.
example.fact: The human eye can resolve detail down to roughly 60 pixels per degree of vision, a benchmark display makers call 'retina' resolution. A clear image viewed at typical reading distance on a modern phone screen already exceeds what the eye alone can distinguish.

components.note: 丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.hanzi: 主教在教堂主持了婚礼。
example.pinyin: Zhǔjiào zài jiàotáng zhǔchí le hūnlǐ.
example.english: The bishop officiated the wedding at the church.
example.fact: St. Nicholas of Myra, a 4th-century bishop in what is now Turkey, was renowned for secretly giving gifts to the poor, including reportedly dropping coins down chimneys and into shoes. Centuries of retelling across Europe eventually reshaped that generous bishop into the modern figure of Santa Claus.

components.note: 氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone

example.hanzi: 国会正在讨论这项法案。
example.pinyin: Guóhuì zhèngzài tǎolùn zhè xiàng fǎ'àn.
example.english: Congress is discussing this bill.
example.fact: The Magna Carta, sealed by King John of England in 1215, was drafted to limit a monarch's power and guarantee certain legal rights to nobles. Though most of its specific clauses are now obsolete, its principle that even a ruler is bound by law underlies how modern bills and constitutions are written.

components.note: 汉 is a simplified form of 漢, pairing the water radical 氵 with a component that named the river valley tied to the Han dynasty and Han Chinese identity.
土 (earth) — relates to 城's meaning 'city, wall,' since city walls were built of earth.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — 城 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 汉城是首尔的旧称。
example.pinyin: Hànchéng shì Shǒu'ěr de jiùchēng.
example.english: Hanseong is the old name for Seoul.
example.fact: Seoul has served as a capital city on the banks of the Han River for more than 600 years, since the Joseon Dynasty established it as its capital in 1394. Today the Seoul metropolitan area is home to over 25 million people, roughly half of South Korea's entire population.

components.note: 尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù
纟 (thread) — 绪 originally meant the end of a thread, extending to 'clue, beginnings.'
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to xù's reading, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 系统已经准备就绪。
example.pinyin: Xìtǒng yǐjīng zhǔnbèi jiùxù.
example.english: The system is ready.
example.fact: During Apollo 11's 1969 launch sequence, NASA's countdown ran through a strict checklist confirming every system — fuel, guidance, telemetry — was ready before the final 'T-minus' seconds ticked to zero. That countdown procedure, refined across earlier Mercury and Gemini missions, became the template still used for rocket launches today.

components.note: Roof — shows shelter, a place to stay.
A person resting inside, suggesting lodging for the night.
人 (person) — 舍 originally described the shape of a roof over a person, a dwelling.
舌 (shé) is an exact match for the sound of 舍.

example.hanzi: 大学生通常住在宿舍里。
example.pinyin: Dàxuéshēng tōngcháng zhù zài sùshè lǐ.
example.english: College students usually live in dormitories.
example.fact: Oxford's oldest colleges, founded in the 13th century, originally housed students and tutors together in shared quarters organized much like monasteries, with communal dining halls and chapels. That residential college model, blending living space with study, went on to influence dormitory design at universities worldwide.

components.note: 广 (shelter) pictures a drying shed.
林-shaped strokes below picture hemp fibers hung to dry, giving 麻 its meaning 'hemp.'
Wine — related to alcohol.
Gives the sound zú, related to zuì but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 手术前病人接受了麻醉。
example.pinyin: Shǒushù qián bìngrén jiēshòu le mázuì.
example.english: The patient received anesthesia before the surgery.
example.fact: On October 16, 1846, dentist William Morton administered ether anesthesia during a public surgery at Massachusetts General Hospital, in a room now nicknamed the 'Ether Dome.' The patient felt no pain, and news of the successful demonstration spread across the world within months, transforming surgery from an agonizing last resort into a survivable procedure.

meanings: to tell it as it is

components.note: 宀 (roof) — the traditional form 實 pictured a house filled with strings of coins (毌) and cowrie-shell currency (貝), a home stocked with solid wealth.
The lower portion, simplified from that coins-and-shells element, still carries the sense of substance — together giving 实 its meaning 'real, solid, true, fruit.'
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'
宀 (roof) — the traditional form 實 pictured a house filled with strings of coins (毌) and cowrie-shell currency (貝), a home stocked with solid wealth.
The lower portion, simplified from that coins-and-shells element, still carries the sense of substance — together giving 实 its meaning 'real, solid, true, fruit.'
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō

example.hanzi: 我们应该实话实说，不要隐瞒。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi shíhuà shíshuō, bùyào yǐnmán.
example.english: We should tell the truth and not hide anything.
example.fact: Researchers at the University of Granada found in a 2012 thermal-imaging study that lying triggers a measurable temperature spike around the nose and a drop around the forehead, an effect nicknamed the 'Pinocchio effect.' The tiny, involuntary shift happens too fast for a liar to control, though it requires specialized cameras to detect.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 细 relates to something as fine and thin as silk thread
田 (tián) gives a loose sound connection to 细's reading xì
Plant — links to fungi and mold, once seen as plant-like.
Gives the sound qūn, related to jūn but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 洗手可以减少细菌感染。
example.pinyin: Xǐshǒu kěyǐ jiǎnshǎo xìjūn gǎnrǎn.
example.english: Washing hands can reduce bacterial infection.
example.fact: Dutch tradesman Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first person to observe bacteria, using hand-ground microscope lenses in 1676 to see what he called 'animalcules' swimming in rainwater and plaque scraped from his own teeth. His detailed letters to the Royal Society laid the groundwork for microbiology two centuries before germ theory was formalized.

components.note: 阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'

example.hanzi: 他和队友配合得很好。
example.pinyin: Tā hé duìyǒu pèihé de hěn hǎo.
example.english: He and his teammates coordinated very well.
example.fact: In the 1980 Winter Olympics, a team of American college and amateur players — considered heavy underdogs — beat the dominant Soviet ice hockey squad 4-3 in a match later called the 'Miracle on Ice.' The US team went on to win the gold medal two days later against Finland.

components.note: 义 (yì) gives a sound close to yí, differing only in tone.
口 (a vessel), shown four times — a set of cooking vessels.
犬 (a dog) — guarding the vessels, the source of 器's meaning 'vessel, tool, instrument.'

example.hanzi: 实验室里有很多精密仪器。
example.pinyin: Shíyànshì lǐ yǒu hěnduō jīngmì yíqì.
example.english: There are many precision instruments in the laboratory.
example.fact: The LIGO gravitational-wave detectors use laser beams bounced along 4-kilometer arms to measure distance changes smaller than one ten-thousandth the width of a proton. That extraordinary sensitivity let the instrument directly detect gravitational waves from colliding black holes for the first time in 2015.

components.note: 口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'
口 (mouth) — 味 relates to taste, sensed in the mouth.
未 (wèi) gives the sound — an exact match with 味.

example.hanzi: 他对艺术很有品味。
example.pinyin: Tā duì yìshù hěn yǒu pǐnwèi.
example.english: He has great taste in art.
example.fact: Human tongues carry roughly 10,000 taste buds, each a cluster of receptor cells that gets replaced about every one to two weeks throughout life. That constant turnover means the tongue that tastes a favorite dish today is, cell for cell, not quite the same one that tasted it a month before.

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo
⺮ (bamboo) — early signature tallies and slips were made of bamboo.
佥 (qiān) is an exact match for the sound of 签.

example.hanzi: 每个产品都贴着价格标签。
example.pinyin: Měi gè chǎnpǐn dōu tiē zhe jiàgé biāoqiān.
example.english: Every product has a price tag attached.
example.fact: The first retail barcode was scanned on June 26, 1974, at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio — a 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum, which now sits in the Smithsonian. Barcodes and their price-tag labels went on to become standard on nearly every packaged product sold worldwide.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — represents a home.
各 (each, various) — a person arriving from elsewhere and welcomed under one's roof gave 客 its meaning 'guest, visitor.'
户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 房 is pronounced fáng, a close match

example.hanzi: 这家酒店的客房非常宽敞。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de kèfáng fēicháng kuānchang.
example.english: This hotel's guest rooms are very spacious.
example.fact: The First World Hotel in Genting Highlands, Malaysia, once held the Guinness World Record for the most guest rooms in a single hotel, with over 7,300 rooms under one roof. That's roughly triple the room count of most of the largest hotels in Las Vegas.

components.note: 无 continues the older form 無, which pictured a person holding decorated tassels or sleeves in a ritual dance. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the negation 'not have, without,' and the dance sense dropped away entirely.
口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.

example.hanzi: 他因为无知而做出错误的决定。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi wúzhī ér zuòchū cuòwù de juédìng.
example.english: He made a wrong decision due to ignorance.
example.fact: Psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger described in a 1999 study what's now called the Dunning-Kruger effect: people with the least knowledge or skill in a domain often rate their own competence the highest, because the same ignorance that causes the mistakes also prevents them from recognizing the mistakes.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.

example.hanzi: 她挑选家具很有眼光。
example.pinyin: Tā tiāoxuǎn jiājù hěn yǒu yǎnguāng.
example.english: She has a good eye for choosing furniture.
example.fact: Birds of prey such as hawks and eagles have visual acuity estimated at two to eight times sharper than a human's, thanks to an unusually dense packing of photoreceptor cells in their retinas. A hawk circling high overhead can reportedly spot a small rodent moving in grass hundreds of meters below.

components.note: 毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 请填写这张表格。
example.pinyin: Qǐng tiánxiě zhè zhāng biǎogé.
example.english: Please fill out this form.
example.fact: When Dmitri Mendeleev published his periodic table in 1869, he left gaps for elements he believed must exist but hadn't yet been discovered, and predicted their properties from the table's pattern. Gallium, discovered six years later, matched his prediction so closely that it helped convince skeptical chemists the table was more than a filing system.

components.note: 十 — traditionally read as a great man standing tall.
一 (the two horizontal strokes) — heaven above and earth below, which the king bridges, giving 王 its meaning 'king, monarch.'
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.

example.hanzi: 这个王国有着悠久的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhège wángguó yǒuzhe yōujiǔ de lìshǐ.
example.english: This kingdom has a long history.
example.fact: Since the early 1970s, the Kingdom of Bhutan has officially tracked 'Gross National Happiness' alongside economic output, weighing factors like community vitality, culture, and environmental health in national policy decisions. It remains one of the only countries to enshrine a happiness index directly into its constitution.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
亻 (person) — 便 concerns something adjusted to suit a person's needs.

更 (to change, alter) — a person changing something to make it easier or more suitable gave 便 its core meaning 'convenient'; the euphemistic sense 'to relieve oneself, feces' (biàn) grew out of that same idea of convenience.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了病人的大便样本。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le bìngrén de dàbiàn yàngběn.
example.english: The doctor examined the patient's stool sample.
example.fact: A 2013 study found that dung beetles use the Milky Way as a compass, rolling their dung balls in straight lines at night by orienting to the band of starlight overhead. They were the first animal shown to navigate by the galaxy rather than the moon or individual stars.

components.note: 彳 (step/walk) — relates directly to 往's meaning 'to go toward, in the direction of.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound hint — 往 is pronounced wǎng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 他往常都很早起床。
example.pinyin: Tā wǎngcháng dōu hěn zǎo qǐchuáng.
example.english: He usually gets up early.
example.fact: French researcher Michel Siffre spent two months living in a cave in 1962 with no clocks or daylight cues, tracking only how his body felt. His internal clock drifted to a day length of about 24.5 hours, part of the early evidence that the human circadian rhythm runs slightly longer than a calendar day.

components.note: 毛 is a simple pictograph of a tuft of fur or feathers, drawn as a few curling strands — it cannot be broken into smaller meaningful parts.
A drawing of a robe's collar and folded sides, seen from the front.

example.hanzi: 冬天她总是穿毛衣。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān tā zǒngshì chuān máoyī.
example.english: In winter she always wears a sweater.
example.fact: Merino wool fibers can absorb up to roughly 30 percent of their own weight in moisture before feeling wet to the touch, while still trapping air to insulate against cold. That combination of warmth and breathability is why merino sweaters are prized for both winter wear and high-exertion outdoor gear.

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè

example.hanzi: 老朋友见面格外亲热。
example.pinyin: Lǎo péngyou jiànmiàn géwài qīnrè.
example.english: Old friends were especially affectionate when they met.
example.fact: Physical affection such as hugging triggers the release of oxytocin, a hormone first isolated in 1906 that lowers stress hormones and blood pressure in both the giver and receiver of the embrace. Oxytocin release also spikes during childbirth and breastfeeding, which is why it's often nicknamed the 'bonding hormone.'

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 请把这张图片放大一些。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng túpiàn fàngdà yīxiē.
example.english: Please enlarge this picture a bit.
example.fact: The Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, has captured images of galaxies more than 13 billion light-years away by gathering and magnifying faint light that left its source before the Earth even existed. Its Deep Field images, made by staring at a single patch of seemingly empty sky for days, revealed thousands of previously invisible galaxies.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
阝 (a mound/place) — relates to 际's meaning 'border, between,' an edge or boundary marker.
示 (shì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了星际旅行的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshù le xīngjì lǚxíng de gùshì.
example.english: This movie tells a story about interstellar travel.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched by NASA in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn, became the first human-made object to cross into interstellar space in 2012, roughly 11 billion miles from the sun. It's still transmitting data today, powered by a slowly decaying plutonium generator expected to run out sometime in the 2030s.

components.note: 木 (tree) — evokes something rising up and standing above the rest, as a tall tree stands out in a forest.
灬 (fire, brightness) — combined with the tree above, the blazing brightness suggested brilliance and distinction, giving 杰 its meaning 'outstanding, heroic.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 她是一位杰出的科学家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi jiéchū de kēxuéjiā.
example.english: She is an outstanding scientist.
example.fact: Marie Curie remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — Physics in 1903 for her work on radioactivity, and Chemistry in 1911 for discovering the elements polonium and radium. She did much of that pioneering research in a converted shed, without the safety equipment that her own findings would later make standard.

components.note: 氐 (dī) gives the sound — 低 is also pronounced dī, an exact match
讠 (speech) — relates to 调's meaning 'to adjust, transfer,' something coordinated through spoken negotiation.
周 (zhōu) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from diào.

example.hanzi: 他为人低调，很少接受采访。
example.pinyin: Tā wéirén dīdiào, hěn shǎo jiēshòu cǎifǎng.
example.english: He keeps a low profile and rarely gives interviews.
example.fact: Eighteenth-century scientist Henry Cavendish, who discovered hydrogen and precisely measured the density of the Earth, was so famously reclusive that he reportedly communicated with his own servants through written notes rather than speak to them directly. Much of his unpublished research on electricity was only discovered and recognized decades after his death.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — the original meaning of 耶 is unrelated to its modern use, which is mainly phonetic.
阝 (a place-name element) gives a sound distantly related to yé, having drifted apart over time.
鱼 (fish) forms the top of the character.
日, placed beneath the fish, was linked to the idea of speaking crudely or bluntly, giving 鲁 its meaning 'rash, uncouth.'

example.hanzi: 他被耶鲁大学录取了。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi Yēlǔ Dàxué lùqǔ le.
example.english: He was admitted to Yale University.
example.fact: Founded in 1701, Yale is the third-oldest institution of higher education in the United States. Its Beinecke Rare Book Library holds one of only about 50 surviving complete copies of the Gutenberg Bible, the first major book printed in Europe with movable type.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 棕 names the palm tree, and the brown color associated with its fiber.
宗 (zōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 棕.
木 (tree) — 榈 names a type of tree, the palm.
闾 (lǘ) gives the sound — an exact match with 榈's reading.

example.hanzi: 海边种着很多棕榈树。
example.pinyin: Hǎibiān zhòng zhe hěnduō zōnglǚ shù.
example.english: Many palm trees are planted by the seaside.
example.fact: Coconut palms produce seeds so buoyant and salt-tolerant that they can float across entire oceans and still germinate after drifting for over 100 days at sea. That built-in seaworthiness is how coconut palms spread naturally to remote tropical islands long before humans ever planted them there.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'
匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.
A stylized foot (related to 止, 'to stop/foot') — originally meant 'to go,' later grammaticalized into a literary possessive/linking particle, similar to 的.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 除此之外，他还学过法语。
example.pinyin: Chú cǐ zhī wài, tā hái xué guò Fǎyǔ.
example.english: Besides this, he has also studied French.
example.fact: The Rosetta Stone, carved in 196 BC, records the same royal decree in three scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Egyptian demotic, and ancient Greek. Because scholars could already read Greek, the stone gave French scholar Jean-François Champollion the key that let him decipher hieroglyphic writing in 1822, unlocking millennia of Egyptian history.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 急 relates to an anxious or urgent state of mind
刍 (chú) gives a sound distantly related to 急's reading jí, having drifted apart over time
讠 (speech) — 诊 describes a doctor asking questions and speaking with a patient to diagnose an illness.
㐱 (zhěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 诊.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì

example.hanzi: 他被送进了急诊室。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi sòng jìn le jízhěnshì.
example.english: He was rushed into the emergency room.
example.fact: Trauma surgeon R Adams Cowley popularized the concept of the 'golden hour' in the 1970s, the idea that a severely injured patient's odds of survival are highest if they reach definitive care within about 60 minutes of injury. The concept reshaped how emergency rooms and ambulance systems prioritize speed for trauma cases.

components.note: 比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 一个字节等于八个比特。
example.pinyin: Yī gè zìjié děngyú bā gè bǐtè.
example.english: One byte equals eight bits.
example.fact: Mathematician and engineer Claude Shannon coined the term 'bit,' short for 'binary digit,' in his 1948 paper 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication,' which founded the field of information theory. His framework for measuring information in bits underlies essentially all digital communication and storage used today.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 婚 relates to marriage, historically centered on the wife.
昏 (hūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婚.
纟 (thread) — 纱 names a type of light, thin fabric, gauze.
少 (shǎo) gives a sound close to shā, sharing the same initial with a different rhyme and tone.

example.hanzi: 新娘穿着白色的婚纱。
example.pinyin: Xīnniáng chuānzhuó báisè de hūnshā.
example.english: The bride wore a white wedding dress.
example.fact: White wedding dresses became fashionable largely after Queen Victoria wore one, rather than the traditional royal silver, at her 1840 wedding to Prince Albert. Before that, brides of most backgrounds commonly wore whatever good dress they owned, in any color, so it could be reused afterward.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坦 describes flat, level ground.
旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to tǎn, sharing a related rhyme.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 一辆坦克缓缓驶过。
example.pinyin: Yī liàng tǎnkè huǎnhuǎn shǐguò.
example.english: A tank slowly drove past.
example.fact: The first tanks saw combat at the Battle of the Somme in September 1916, and were code-named 'tanks' during development and shipping so that factory workers and spies would mistake the crates for water-storage containers headed to Russia. The disguise name stuck even after the vehicles' true purpose became obvious on the battlefield.

components.note: 风's oldest form was written identically to 鳳 (phoenix), a mythical wind-bringing bird; ancient scribes used that bird image as a rebus for the abstract idea of 'wind.' Over time the two characters split apart, and the simplified 风 came to enclose 虫 (a small creature), pictured as stirred up and carried along by the moving air.
走 (to walk/run) — 趣 originally related to hurrying eagerly toward something, extending to 'interesting, of interest.'
取 (qǔ) gives a sound close to qù, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 他说话很风趣，大家都喜欢和他聊天。
example.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà hěn fēngqù, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan hé tā liáotiān.
example.english: He is witty when he speaks, and everyone likes chatting with him.
example.fact: Mark Twain's sharp, understated wit made him one of the most quoted writers in the English language, with lines still repeated more than a century after his death in 1910. He reportedly kept a running scrapbook of clippings and notes just to track his own jokes and observations for reuse.

components.note: 自 here depicts a head (the character also independently means 'nose, self').
丷 depicts hair atop the head — 首 originally pictured a head with hair, giving its meaning 'head, chief, first.'
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'

example.hanzi: 英国首相住在唐宁街十号。
example.pinyin: Yīngguó shǒuxiàng zhù zài Tángníng Jiē shí hào.
example.english: The British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street.
example.fact: Winston Churchill is the only British Prime Minister to have won a Nobel Prize in Literature rather than Peace, awarded in 1953 largely for his historical writing and wartime speeches. He had been nominated for the Peace Prize multiple times over the years but never won it.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诞 originally described boastful, exaggerated speech.
延 (yán) gives a sound distantly related to dàn, having drifted apart over time.
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 这个理论诞生于二十世纪初。
example.pinyin: Zhège lǐlùn dànshēng yú èrshí shìjì chū.
example.english: This theory was born in the early 20th century.
example.fact: The World Wide Web was born between 1989 and 1991, when physicist Tim Berners-Lee, working at CERN, wrote the first web browser, the first web server, and the first webpage to help researchers share documents. Fewer than a dozen websites existed by the end of 1992; today there are well over a billion.

components.note: 匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 传说中死神会带走逝者的灵魂。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō zhōng sǐshén huì dàizǒu shìzhě de línghún.
example.english: Legend says death takes away the souls of the deceased.
example.fact: The hooded, scythe-carrying 'Grim Reaper' image took shape in European art during and after the Black Death of 1347-1351, a plague that killed an estimated 25 to 50 million people, roughly a third of Europe's population. Constant, visible mortality on that scale pushed death itself into becoming a recurring, personified figure in paintings and woodcuts of the era.

components.note: 金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

example.hanzi: 夕阳把天空染成了金色。
example.pinyin: Xīyáng bǎ tiānkōng rǎnchéng le jīnsè.
example.english: The setting sun dyed the sky golden.
example.fact: Gold is so chemically unreactive that it almost never corrodes or tarnishes, which is why an estimated 244,000 tonnes of gold ever mined throughout human history — nearly all of it — still exists today in some form, from jewelry to coins to circuit boards. Melted down, all of it would fit into a cube roughly 22 meters on each side.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 适 relates to fitting well as one moves along, i.e. being suitable
舌 (shé) gives a sound distantly related to 适's reading shì, having drifted apart over a long time

The simplified 当 fuses together what was originally 當: 尚 (to esteem, held up high) written above 田 (a field). Two plots of farmland judged to be of matching, esteemed value gave 當/当 its meanings 'to correspond to, be equal to; ought to.'

example.hanzi: 请选择适当的时间开会。
example.pinyin: Qǐng xuǎnzé shìdàng de shíjiān kāihuì.
example.english: Please choose an appropriate time for the meeting.
example.fact: Astronomers use the term 'Goldilocks zone' for the orbital region around a star where temperatures are just right for liquid water to exist on a planet's surface — not too hot, not too cold. The term borrows from the children's story and has become standard shorthand in the search for potentially habitable exoplanets.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 忠 describes a heart that stays true, loyalty.
中 (zhōng) is an exact match for the sound of 忠.
宀 (roof) — the traditional form 實 pictured a house filled with strings of coins (毌) and cowrie-shell currency (貝), a home stocked with solid wealth.
The lower portion, simplified from that coins-and-shells element, still carries the sense of substance — together giving 实 its meaning 'real, solid, true, fruit.'

example.hanzi: 狗是人类忠实的朋友。
example.pinyin: Gǒu shì rénlèi zhōngshí de péngyǒu.
example.english: Dogs are humans' faithful friends.
example.fact: In 1920s Tokyo, an Akita dog named Hachikō continued walking to Shibuya Station every day for nearly ten years after his owner died suddenly at work, waiting for a return that never came. A bronze statue of Hachikō still stands outside the station today, and the story remains one of Japan's best-known examples of animal loyalty.

meanings: to enjoy (i.e. have the use or benefit of)

components.note: 亠 (a roof) — the top of a house.
口 (a mouth) — eating and enjoying inside it.
子 (a child) — together showing a family living and eating well under one roof, giving 享 its meaning 'to enjoy.'

用 is generally read as a pictograph of a wooden pail, cask, or fenced enclosure used for storing or drawing something — a container put into service, which gave the character its meaning 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 我们在花园里享用晚餐。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huāyuán lǐ xiǎngyòng wǎncān.
example.english: We enjoyed dinner in the garden.
example.fact: The formal 'service à la russe' dining style, which serves courses to guests one at a time in sequence rather than piling every dish onto the table at once, spread through European aristocratic banquets in the 19th century. That sequential format is the direct ancestor of the multi-course restaurant meal most diners enjoy today.

meanings: to indicate clearly and with certainty

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 老师指定他为班长。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhǐdìng tā wéi bānzhǎng.
example.english: The teacher appointed him class monitor.
example.fact: In the Roman Republic, a dictator was a legally appointed office, not an illegitimate seizure of power — the Senate could designate one person with sweeping emergency authority, but strictly for a fixed term of six months. That built-in expiration was meant to prevent exactly the kind of permanent one-man rule the word later came to mean.
